# Third-party notices

`Sources/AU05Device/Protocol.swift` adapts report encryption/decryption, command formats and physical button identifiers from [AU05 Keys](https://github.com/elliclee/ulanzi-au05-keys), revision `7819351a5ba5c68874d0519fabe3bf62db47e328` (`Battery.swift`, `VendorKeys.swift`, `Core.swift`). Copyright (c) 2026 AU05 Keys contributors. The complete MIT license is retained in [AU05-Keys-LICENSE](AU05-Keys-LICENSE) and included in app bundles.

The native HID transport and lifecycle are implemented here. No Ulanzi proprietary binary or firmware is distributed.

The optional DualSense microphone helper bundles libopus from [Opus / Xiph.Org](https://opus-codec.org/). Its upstream [copyright and license notices](Opus-COPYING.txt) are retained here and shipped in the app resources as `Opus-COPYING.txt`. These third-party notices remain independent of VibeWand's own license, the GNU GPL 3.0 in [`LICENSE`](../LICENSE).

Command mode's kernel is assembled by `scripts/build-kernel.sh` and shipped in the app under `Contents/Resources/kernel`; none of it is stored in this repository.

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24.21.0, the official Apple Silicon build, unmodified and with its original signature. Its license, which also covers the libraries built into it, ships as `kernel/node/LICENSE`.
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 0.2.0-rc.2 (MIT), limited to the packages VibeWand's coordinator bundle names (`kernel/coordinator/package.json`), the launcher's own support packages and, since 0.10.0, its SenseVoice plug-in (`kernel/package.json`), together with the dependencies recorded in `kernel/package-lock.json`. Among those is its multi-provider model component, which builds on [pi-ai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-ai) (MIT) and on the SDKs of the services it can reach: OpenAI (Apache-2.0), Anthropic (MIT), Google Gen AI (Apache-2.0) and AWS (Apache-2.0).
- Installed on Apple Silicon, the kernel holds 222 packages besides VibeWand's own bundle. 79 are DeepSeek Harness's own, MIT apart from two under BSD-3-Clause. The other 143 come from third parties, under the MIT (83), Apache-2.0 (40), BSD-3-Clause (12), ISC (4), 0BSD, Python-2.0, Unlicense and LGPL-3.0-or-later (one each) licenses. Each names its license in its own `package.json` inside `kernel/node_modules`, and all but twelve also carry the license text there. The twelve are the two sherpa-onnx packages and the prebuilt libvips, both described below, and nine packages published without a license file of their own, listed after this paragraph. An earlier wording of this notice gave 216 as the number of third-party packages; that figure counted the harness's own packages too.
  - `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-http` 3.972.74, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-login` 3.972.79 and `@aws-sdk/nested-clients` 3.997.46 (Apache-2.0): [AWS-SDK-for-JavaScript-LICENSE](AWS-SDK-for-JavaScript-LICENSE), the `LICENSE` of [aws/aws-sdk-js-v3](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-js-v3), which has no `NOTICE` file.
  - `@earendil-works/pi-ai` and `@earendil-works/pi-telemetry` 0.87.1 (MIT): [pi-LICENSE](pi-LICENSE), the `LICENSE` of [earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) at `v0.87.1`.
  - `@koromix/koffi-darwin-arm64` 3.1.1 (MIT): its text is the `LICENSE.txt` of the `koffi` package of the same version, which ships beside it in `kernel/node_modules/koffi`.
  - `data-uri-to-buffer` 4.0.1 (MIT): the full text is in the package's own `README.md`.
  - `standardwebhooks` 1.1.1: its `package.json` says MIT, while the one license file in [its repository](https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks) is the Apache License 2.0, kept as [standard-webhooks-LICENSE](standard-webhooks-LICENSE). The project publishes no MIT text for the package.
  - `proxy-agent-negotiate` 1.1.0 (MIT by its `package.json`): neither the package nor its folder in [TooTallNate/proxy-agents](https://github.com/TooTallNate/proxy-agents) holds a license text, so there is none to keep. `agent-base`, by the same author from the same repository, ships his MIT text in `kernel/node_modules/agent-base/LICENSE`.
- Dictation's SenseVoice service runs the recogniser of the harness's SenseVoice plug-in (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-speech-to-text-sensevoice`, MIT). The plug-in uses [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) 1.13.8 (Apache-2.0): the package `sherpa-onnx-node` and the prebuilt `sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64`, shipped unmodified under `kernel/node_modules`, about 34 MB, and loaded only while SenseVoice recognises a recording. Neither package carries a license text, so the texts are kept here and shipped in the app resources: sherpa-onnx's license as [sherpa-onnx-LICENSE](sherpa-onnx-LICENSE), and for the prebuilt package's `libonnxruntime.dylib`, which is [ONNX Runtime](https://onnxruntime.ai) 1.28.2 (MIT, Microsoft Corporation), its license as [ONNX-Runtime-LICENSE](ONNX-Runtime-LICENSE) with the notices for the libraries built into it as [ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt](ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt). The three are the files of those versions as their projects publish them. This is new in 0.10.0.
- The prebuilt package's `libsherpa-onnx-c-api.dylib` has more than sherpa-onnx built into it. sherpa-onnx's build files for 1.13.8 (the `cmake` folder of its repository, and kaldi-decoder's for kaldifst) name the libraries and the revisions used, and the file that ships holds code of each:
  - kaldi-native-fbank 1.22.3, kaldi-decoder 0.3.0 and simple-sentencepiece 0.7 (Apache-2.0). Their `LICENSE` files are the text kept as `sherpa-onnx-LICENSE`, and none of them has a `NOTICE` file.
  - kaldifst 1.8.0 (Apache-2.0): [kaldifst-LICENSE](kaldifst-LICENSE), which opens with the project's note on who holds its copyright.
  - OpenFst, in the fork `csukuangfj/openfst` at `v1.8.5-2026-07-09` (Apache-2.0, Copyright 2005-2026 Google LLC): [OpenFst-COPYING](OpenFst-COPYING).
  - JSON for Modern C++ 3.12.0 (MIT): [JSON-for-Modern-Cpp-LICENSE.MIT](JSON-for-Modern-Cpp-LICENSE.MIT).
  - hclust-cpp, in the fork `csukuangfj/hclust-cpp` at `2026-02-25` (BSD-2-Clause): [hclust-cpp-LICENSE](hclust-cpp-LICENSE).
  - piper-phonemize, in the fork `csukuangfj/piper-phonemize` at `f3ff95af` (MIT): [piper-phonemize-LICENSE.md](piper-phonemize-LICENSE.md).
  - Eigen 5.0.1 (MPL-2.0), source at [libeigen/eigen](https://gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen).
  - [eSpeak NG](https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng) for speech synthesis, in the fork `csukuangfj/espeak-ng`, under **GPL-3.0-or-later**. VibeWand only recognises speech and never calls the synthesis code, but that code is in the library as published, and the library ships as it is. VibeWand is under the GNU GPL 3.0 itself, so the text of that license is VibeWand's own [`LICENSE`](../LICENSE), which ships in the app resources. The other notices eSpeak NG carries are kept as [eSpeak-NG-COPYING.APACHE](eSpeak-NG-COPYING.APACHE), [eSpeak-NG-COPYING.BSD2](eSpeak-NG-COPYING.BSD2) and [eSpeak-NG-COPYING.UCD](eSpeak-NG-COPYING.UCD). Its source at the revision built in is [csukuangfj/espeak-ng at `ed530aa1`](https://github.com/csukuangfj/espeak-ng/tree/ed530aa113046142eb5115cf2fc9157854d0ffe1).

  The source the whole library is built from is [sherpa-onnx at `v1.13.8`](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/tree/v1.13.8); its `cmake` folder fetches each library above at the revision named here. All of these texts ship in the app resources under `third-party`.
- The models SenseVoice needs are not part of the app and are not stored in this repository. When the user asks for them, VibeWand downloads the files the plug-in pins from Hugging Face or its mirror: SenseVoiceSmall as converted for sherpa-onnx (`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17`, from [FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice)) and Silero VAD (`csukuangfj/vad`, from [snakers4/silero-vad](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad), MIT). The original model, [FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall](https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall), is published by Alibaba Group under the [FunASR Model Open Source License Agreement 1.1](https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR/blob/main/MODEL_LICENSE), which asks whoever uses or shares it to name the source and author and to keep the model's name. The VAD file the plug-in pins (1,807,522 bytes, SHA-256 `a35ebf52fd3ce5f1469b2a36158dba761bc47b973ea3382b3186ca15b1f5af28`) is byte for byte `files/silero_vad.onnx` of snakers4/silero-vad at its tag `v4.0`, Copyright (c) 2020-present Silero Team; the repository `csukuangfj/vad` it is fetched from states no license of its own. VibeWand names both models, their authors and their terms where it offers the download, in Settings and in the first-run guide.
- The harness's picture store (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local`), which holds a picture a tool shows the model, uses [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com) 0.35.5 (Apache-2.0) and with it the prebuilt [libvips](https://www.libvips.org) for Apple Silicon, `@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64` 1.3.4, under **LGPL-3.0-or-later**. It is one dynamic library, `kernel/node_modules/@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64/lib/libvips-cpp.8.18.7.dylib`, shipped unmodified, loaded only when the model is shown a picture, and replaceable with a build of your own. The `README.md` beside it lists every library built into it with its license (among them glib, pango, librsvg, libheif, libexif and fribidi under the LGPL, cairo under the MPL 1.1), `versions.json` gives their versions, and the build recipes with pointers to the sources are at [lovell/sharp-libvips](https://github.com/lovell/sharp-libvips). This is new in 0.10.0. The package carries neither license text, so both ship in the app resources: the GNU LGPL 3.0 as [GNU-LGPL-3.0.txt](GNU-LGPL-3.0.txt), and the GPL 3.0 it builds on as VibeWand's own [`LICENSE`](../LICENSE).

  **Using a libvips of your own.** Build it from those recipes or from your changed source, keeping the name `libvips-cpp.8.18.7.dylib` and the interface of libvips 8.18 that sharp 0.35.5 links (`@rpath/libvips-cpp.8.18.7.dylib`). Put it in place of the file above inside `VibeWand.app`, then sign the app again, because changing a file inside the bundle breaks its signature:

  ```sh
  codesign --force --sign - --identifier org.vibewand.bridge /Applications/VibeWand.app
  ```

  macOS ties the permissions it has granted VibeWand, such as Accessibility and the microphone, to that signature, so it may ask for them again. Checked on 0.11.0 with the same library signed differently standing in for a rebuilt one: the bundle then fails `codesign --verify`, verifies again after the command, and the bundled Node loads sharp through the changed file.

**Open items.** The questions still undecided, device artwork and the key constants of the AU05 protocol among them, are listed with what was settled and how in [`docs/licensing-open-items.md`](../docs/licensing-open-items.md) of the repository.

VibeWand's coordinator bundle (`kernel/coordinator`, installed in the kernel as the package `vibewand-coordinator`) is part of VibeWand. The same bundle, and the overlay beside it (`kernel/overlay`), ship as `Contents/Resources/harness/` for a DeepSeek Harness the user installed themselves. In that mode nothing of the harness is shipped or modified: the user's own installation runs it.
